blogs.title: Why Finetuning Massive Foundation Models is So Tough – And How Orthogonal Finetuning Offers a Solution
blogs.description: An accessible overview of the challenges of adapting gigantic pretrained models, why naive finetuning can destroy learned knowledge, and how Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) preserves relational geometry between neurons to keep the model’s original capabilities intact.

blogs.title: From Fast Fourier Transform to AI: The Butterfly Structure That Makes BOFT Parameter‑Efficient
blogs.description: Explains the butterfly factorization originally used in the Cooley‑Tukey FFT algorithm, how it creates dense orthogonal matrices from sparse components, and why this clever graph‑based information transmission reduces trainable parameters from O(d²) to O(d log d).

blogs.title: BOFT 101: A Gentle Introduction to Parameter‑Efficient Orthogonal Finetuning
blogs.description: Breaks down the new BOFT method step‑by‑step—starting from orthogonal matrix basics, moving through butterfly components, and showing how they combine into a compact yet expressive transformation for any linear layer.

blogs.title: Preserving Angles and Spectral Norms: The Mathematics Behind BOFT’s Strong Generalization
blogs.description: Dives into the core theoretical insights—how orthogonal updates keep pairwise neuron angles unchanged, maintain the spectral norm of pretrained weights, and why this leads to more stable training compared to low‑rank approaches like LoRA.

blogs.title: Benchmarking BOFT: Real‑World Gains on Vision Transformers, Large Language Models, and Diffusion Systems
blogs.description: Summarizes the extensive experiments from the paper, highlighting how BOFT outperforms state‑of‑the‑art PEFT methods across vision, language, and text‑to‑image tasks while using far fewer trainable parameters.

blogs.title: Practical Guide: Adding BOFT to Your Model Adaptation Toolbox
blogs.description: Provides a step‑by‑step recipe for implementing BOFT in popular frameworks (PyTorch/Transformers), discusses initialization tricks (identity via Cayley transform), multiplicative dropout tricks, and when to choose BOFT over adapters or LoRA.

blogs.title: Beyond Butterflies: The Information Transmission View of Parameter‑Efficient Finetuning
blogs.description: Explores the novel graph‑theoretic perspective introduced in the paper—visualizing sparse orthogonal factorizations as information flows on grid graphs—and hints at future network topologies that could further improve efficiency.
